text:
Maya Thompson: Heads up everyone 14 — new Dependent Travel Stipend going live 2026-05-01. This is an add-on to our travel policy to help cover reasonable dependent care or travel when you must bring a dependent on short business trips. Full addendum: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/dependent-travel (TL;DR below)

Diego Ramos: Nice! What counts as a dependent for this?

Maya Thompson: Dependents = children under 13, elderly dependents living in your household, or a dependent with documented medical needs. Youll need a brief note in the claim to explain the dependency (no medical records required, just a statement).

Nia Carter: Quick bullets so folks can skim: 1) Up to $500 per qualifying trip for dependent travel or short-term caregiving costs (per-trip cap). 2) Annual max $1,000 per employee, use-it-or-lose-it by calendar year. 3) Emergency bridge support: up to $200/day for up to 3 consecutive days if regular care falls through while traveling. 4) Eligible: FT employees and PT employees with >=0.6 FTE. Contractors and temps excluded (exception pathway available).

Owen Li: How do we submit? Concur or Expensify?

Maya Thompson: Were using Expensify for this rollout to speed approvals (expense code DEP-TRAV). Concur will remain our default for regular travel. Submit: Expenses -> New -> DEP-TRAV, attach receipts and a one-line justification tying the expense to the business trip.

Samir (Legal): A few legal/tax notes: 1) For US employees, reimbursements under $1,000/year are generally non-taxable when theyre for bona fide business-related dependent care tied to travel; Payroll will run an exception review per-claim. 2) For non-US jurisdictions, tax treatment varies 0% rule not applicable everywhere — Payroll will tag items for tax review. If you need country-specific guidance, include the payroll region in your expense note.

Diego Ramos: Are we covering visas, extra plane tickets for dependents, or only daycare/hotel nights?

Maya Thompson: Policy covers reasonable travel & care costs directly tied to bringing or caring for a dependent on a business trip (e.g., an extra airfare leg, short-term childcare, or hotel nights for the dependent). Visa/immigration costs are excluded unless pre-approved by People Ops for mission-critical travel — contact us in advance.

Nia Carter: Retroactivity?

Maya Thompson: Claims for travel on or after 2026-05-01 only. If you had an urgent trip between 2026-04-15 and 2026-04-30, submit a case to people-ops@redwood.com and well review exceptions.

Owen Li: Edge case: I work in EMEA and the dependent requires a medical note which is sensitive info. How do we handle that?

Samir (Legal): Dont upload medical records. A manager-certified statement is sufficient for eligibility checks. People Ops will treat any health info as sensitive and handle it via secure channels; only the small team doing eligibility checks will see it.

Payroll Team: Note for submitters: include a currency conversion screenshot if receipts arent in company default currency. Expensify will accept EUR/GBP/JPY receipts but tag them for review. Payroll will flag entries for country tax treatment if the employee is non-US.

Maya Thompson: Implementation timeline: - May 1: policy effective and Expensify form live. - May 1May 15: parallel support available via People Ops for first-time claimants. - June: well review utilization and consider adjustments to caps.

Nia Carter: Any manager approvals required?

Maya Thompson: Yes, manager sign-off is required for the expense submission. For emergencies outside business hours, submit the claim and tag your manager and people-ops@redwood.com; People Ops can provisionally approve within 48 hours.

Diego Ramos: Can managers see DEP-TRAV spend against their team budgets?

Payroll Team: Well report DEP-TRAV as a separate ledger line and it will not reduce team travel budgets. Managers will see aggregated DEP-TRAV spend for headcount reporting only.
